record.paper_title: QM2017: Status and Key open Questions in Ultra-Relativistic Heavy-Ion Physics
record.original_question: Can a complete and coherent theory describe quarkonium suppression and regeneration for both J/ψ and Υ families across SPS, RHIC, and LHC energies, including whether sequential Υ melting changes with temperature between RHIC and LHC once lattice-QCD spectral functions, cold nuclear matter effects, energy loss, co-movers, hydrodynamic evolution, heavy-quark diffusion, and feed-down are all included?

evidence.quote: The original deconfinement signal, sequential quarkonia suppression (RAAΥ(1)> Υ(2)> Υ(3)), has been observed at LHC for the Υ family.

Together with RHIC data (and smaller error bars), we may be able to see experimentally the effect of raising the temperature, if the melting pattern of different Υ states would change between the two energies. However, so far it seems that the RAA of Υ is very much comparable at RHIC and LHC (Déjà vu?).

Although the theory description of heavy quark suppression has advanced significantly, a complete and fully coherent description of all quarkonium data (J/ψ and Υ families) at SPS/RHIC/LHC needs significant further work (e.g. to include all of lQCD spectral functions, CNM effects like PDFs, energy loss, co-movers, hydro evolution, heavy quark diffusion, feed-down, ..).

artifact.status_search_result: Recent reviews and modeling efforts (e.g., unified transport-based descriptions and 2024–2025 experimental reviews of quarkonium at the LHC) report substantial progress: unified models combining color screening, gluonic dissociation, collisional damping, and regeneration reproduce many features of sequential suppression for Υ states, and global fits of binding-energy-dependent suppression have been proposed. However, no single framework has yet been demonstrated to coherently describe all J/ψ- and Υ-family observables simultaneously at SPS, RHIC, and LHC with all listed ingredients (lattice spectral functions, CNM effects, energy loss, comovers, hydrodynamics, heavy-quark diffusion, feed-down). The question of whether sequential Υ melting differs between RHIC and LHC remains experimentally and theoretically unresolved, with current R_AA measurements appearing comparable within uncertainties.

status_evidence.title: The fate of quarkonia in heavy-ion collisions at LHC energies: a unified description of the sequential suppression patterns
status_evidence.snippet: A single parameter computed through a global fit of all available suppression patterns fully determines the hierarchy of nuclear effects for all states and centrality bins.
status_evidence.claim: Unified phenomenological descriptions of sequential quarkonium suppression have been developed but rely on simplified, parameter-driven fits rather than a fully microscopic coherent theory.

status_evidence.title: Experimental Review of the Quarkonium Physics at the LHC
status_evidence.snippet: Sequential suppression of Υ(1S), Υ(2S), Υ(3S) observed; theoretical modeling continues to be refined.
status_evidence.claim: As of recent reviews, a fully coherent global theory across SPS/RHIC/LHC for both charmonium and bottomonium remains a work in progress.

status_evidence.title: An experimental review of open heavy flavor and quarkonium production at RHIC
status_evidence.snippet: Comparison of Υ R_AA at RHIC and LHC shows comparable suppression within uncertainties.
status_evidence.claim: Experimental data have not yet conclusively distinguished sequential Υ melting patterns between RHIC and LHC energies.
